key_insight: NH4SCN enables high-n quasi-2D perovskite scaffolds to template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, suggesting its benefit arises from improved 3D structure rather than charge transport through vertical 2D layers.
engineering_relevance: Additive-controlled crystallization offers a route to improve perovskite film ordering, provided the quasi-2D scaffold and 3D phase have compatible lattices.
method: Probe crystallization using spectroscopic and structural studies.
Use NH4SCN to extend the nucleation window, suppress n = 1 phases, and promote high-n scaffolds.
Assess lattice matching and cation-dependent structural templating.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, but provides no quantitative device-performance metrics.
watch_item: The templating effect is cation dependent and requires both close lattice matching and effective kinetic control of quasi-2D phase formation.
paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
